criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies government conflates Fund IV and Fund V election timing for TY 2020
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue A-1 quotes the brief's claim that both TY 2020 elections were executed after the year began, and shows the Fund IV election was signed December 10, 2019 while only the Fund V election (January 28, 2020) was late.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes that the error affects $10,362,000 of $16,362,000 in TY 2020 waivers
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo limits the timing argument to the $6,000,000 Fund V election and quantifies $41,612,000 (87.4%) as prospective. The election table lists the Fund IV TY 2020 waiver at $10,362,000 as timely.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies omission of factor (4) from § 1.707-2(c) six-factor test
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-2 says the brief skips Factor (4) of the § 1.707-2(c) test entirely and puts a different heading in its place.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies conflation of § 707 disguised payment analysis with § 704(b) SEE rules
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-2 identifies that the brief imports the § 704(b) transitory-allocation / substantial economic effect framework in place of the § 707(a)(2)(A) factor analysis, and explains that the two frameworks are distinct.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies incorrect aggregate tax benefit figure of $9,530,400
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue C-1 and Part III.B flag the $9,530,400 aggregate tax benefit as wrong.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Provides correct calculation of $8,094,040 using government's own figures
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo shows $47,612,000 x 17% = $8,094,040 and notes the overstatement of $1,436,360.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Notes the $9,530,400 implies ~20% differential, suggesting unstated NIIT assumption or math error
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo says $9,530,400 equals 20% of a different base ($47,652,000). It mentions the 3.8% NIIT only to say both figures ignore it, never as a possible explanation for the inflated figure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies mischaracterization of Rev. Proc. 93-27
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-1 quotes the brief's and Ashford's 'taxed at receipt if determinable value' statement about Rev. Proc. 93-27 and identifies it as a mischaracterization.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: States correct holding of Rev. Proc. 93-27
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo states that Rev. Proc. 93-27 § 4.01 treats receipt of a profits interest for services as not a taxable event, subject to exceptions including a substantially certain and predictable income stream.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies contradiction re Fund V having 'substantial capital gains activity'
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue A-3 contrasts the brief's 'substantial capital gains activity' claim with Quillen Ex. 4: zero realized gains and unrealized appreciation later written down. The memo also notes deployment of only $380M of $1.75B.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Notes the $6M priority allocation from Fund V was never funded by realized gains
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo notes that the $6,000,000 Fund V allocation could not be satisfied from realized gains, was carried forward and remained unsatisfied, so HCP received nothing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Notes nuance that this contradiction could both help and hurt the government
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo treats Fund V's lack of realized gains as purely favorable to HCP (evidence of real risk). It never acknowledges that this fact could support the government's argument that the allocation was illusory or lacked economic substance; the D-8 caveat concerns a different issue, HCP's reporting.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies government applied only subjective prong of economic substance doctrine
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-6 states the brief's economic substance analysis is almost entirely about purpose and never analyzes the objective prong under § 7701(o)(1)(A).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Cites IRC § 7701(o) conjunctive two-prong test requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo cites § 7701(o) and discusses each prong, but never explains that the codified test is conjunctive, requiring both prongs to be satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Flags statute of limitations vulnerability for TY 2018
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-14 notes the TY 2018 return was filed September 15, 2019 and the FPAA issued June 15, 2022, and says the three-year § 6235(a) period ran September 15, 2022, so the FPAA was within the period only if valid.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Notes government brief's silence on limitations is a strategic vulnerability
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo flags that the brief has no discussion of §§ 6231 or 6235 and calls the failure to address timeliness a gap. It directs investigation of any § 6235 extension and pleading of limitations, which treats the silence as a vulnerability to exploit.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies terminological error — 'Tax Matters Partner' vs. 'Partnership Representative'
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue A-9 identifies the brief's TEFRA term 'Tax Matters Partner' and says BBA years require a partnership representative.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies factual error — Sato named but Hargrove was designated Partnership Rep
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue A-9 notes the brief names Diane K. Sato as Tax Matters Partner, while Ex. 7 (the TY 2018 Form 1065) designates Elliot R. Hargrove as Partnership Representative.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Notes potential impact on validity of notices/procedural steps
criteria_results.reasoning: Issues A-9 and B-14 link the misidentification to the procedural validity of the FPA and notices (mailed to the partnership representative) and to a possible limitations defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies that Pinnacle Partners is distinguishable on its facts
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-4 identifies Pinnacle Partners as the government's only fee-waiver case and shows it is distinguishable on its facts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies the specific distinguishing fact — deficit restoration obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-4 identifies the deficit restoration obligation as the decisive fact, shown in the government's own Exhibit 12, and notes HCP has no DRO.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies internal contradiction — carried interest vs. guaranteed payments
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue C-2 identifies that Arg. IV.B ('economically indistinguishable from carried interest') contradicts Part V.A ('guaranteed payments' under § 707(c)).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Explains why carried interest and guaranteed payment characterizations are inconsistent
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo explains that carried interest is a distributive share taxed as capital gain, while a § 707(c) payment is by definition independent of partnership income, so the characterizations cannot both be true.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies government asserts § 6662 penalty without addressing reasonable cause
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-11 flags that the brief's § 6662 penalty section ignores the reasonable cause defense under § 6664(c)(1).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References Ridgeline Advisors opinion letter as basis for reasonable cause
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue B-11 cites the November 1, 2017 Ridgeline Opinion, a written 'more likely than not' opinion obtained before implementation, as the basis for reasonable cause.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Notes reliance on professional tax advice as recognized defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo states that reliance on professional advice qualifies as reasonable cause, citing Treas. Reg. § 1.6664-4 and Neonatology.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum includes a section flagging non-issues / items not to raise
criteria_results.reasoning: Part VIII, 'Items That Appear Problematic but Should Not Be Raised', lists 13 such items.
